---- Appellant  Versus 1- State Of Chhattisgarh, Through The Station House Officer, Police Station, Batouli, District Surguja (C.G.)
 ---- Respondent For Appellant : Mr. Gurudev I. Sharan, Advocate For Respondent/State : Mr. Dilman Rati Minj,
G.A. Hon'ble Shri Justice Parth Prateem Sahu Order On Board 12/07/2024 1.

Appellant has filed this appeal under Section 14 (A) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 for grant of regular bail as he has been arrested in connection with Crime No.107/2023, registered at Police Station - Batouli, District - Surguja (C.G.) for offence punishable under Section 294, 506, 323, 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3 (2) (v) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

sentences.text: 2. As per report submitted by the Office, notice sent to victim is served, however, there is no representation on her behalf.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:25139 3.

Case of the prosecution in brief is that victim lodged a report in the concerned police station alleging that applicant gave her phone call, asked her to come at particular place on the pretext that his parents wants to meet her.
When she reached at the identified place, applicant took her to a lonely place and committed forceful sexual intercourse abused her and also threatened her to withdraw earlier complaint made by her.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for appellant submits that appellant has been falsely implicated in this case only because he has been released on bail in the earlier crime registered by same complainant against applicant to make out the offence more graver.
Allegation levelled by victim, who is married lady on the date of incident, appears to be false and concocted.
Applicant is in jail since 14.04.2024.

Therefore, he may be enlarged on regular bail.
5.
Learned counsel for State opposes the submission of learned counsel for appellant and would submit that as per record complainant has lodged report against applicant for commission of same offence.
In the present case, there is allegation that applicant called her at lonely place and committed sexual intercourse with her and also threatened her to withdraw the earlier complaint made by her.
However, he does not dispute the submission of counsel for applicant that victim is a married lady.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:25139 7.

Considering the submission of learned counsel for respective parties, in particular the submission of learned counsel for parties that victim on the date of incident was a married lady aged about 27 years and as per her statement, she went to meet applicant taking permission from her house,
without commenting anything on merits of the case, I am inclined to allow this appeal.
8. Accordingly, appeal is allowed.
Impugned order passed by learned Court below on 28.05.2024, is set-aside.

It is directed that the appellant shall be released on regular bail upon his furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court below on the conditions that:-
a). Appellant shall appear before the trial Court regularly on each and every date,
unless exempted from appearance.
(b). Appellant shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c). If appellant is found involved in similar offence in the future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of Bail.
Certified copy as per rules.

Sd/-
